_comment: Bought parts of the two crank walkers. class: maker = the maker's own published figure; third-party = a parts catalogue or reseller page; assumed = not published anywhere found, with the reason for the value. Lengths in mm, masses in g, torque in N m.

ev3_brick.name: EV3 Intelligent Brick 45500

size_mm.note: BrickOwl catalogue, 14 x 9 x 4.67 studs. LEGO publishes no outer dimensions. With the rechargeable pack the brick is deeper (LEGO: 'slightly larger'); not modelled.

mass_bare_g.why: LEGO publishes no mass. Retailer listings give 206 to 215 g and may include packaging.

mass_six_aa_g.why: six alkaline AA cells at 23 g each, a typical cell data sheet value

mass_rechargeable_pack_g.why: 45501 pack, 7.4 V lithium ion; no published mass found

ev3_brick.battery_assumed: six AA cells (the retail 31313 set has no rechargeable pack), so 348 g; 310 g with the pack

supply.value: six AA cells or the 7.4 V rechargeable pack

mounting_holes.why: no drawing of the pin holes found; the design straps the brick instead of pinning it

mass_g.why: LEGO publishes none. 76 g is quoted in a third-party book; a reseller lists 82 g with packaging.

no_load_rpm.note: user guide: 'runs at 160-170 rpm'; the middle is used as the no-load speed

encoder.note: the guide states 1-degree resolution for the medium motor; the large motor is taken as the same

hole_pattern.why: no dimensioned drawing found. The output is a cross-axle hole through a hub at one end. Brackets are built around the motor in hand, as the design README says.

envelope.why: two boxes inside the catalogue size: a hub 24 x 24 x 24 mm on the output axis and a body 84 x 39 x 47 mm beyond it

rotor_inertia_kgm2.why: reflected rotor and gear inertia at the output, for the simulation

ev3_medium_motor.name: EV3 Medium Servo Motor 45503 (optional head pan, not modelled)

mass_g.why: LEGO publishes none; 36 g is quoted in a third-party book

angular_motor.name: Technic Medium Angular Motor (Robot Inventor 51515, element 6299646)

mass_g.why: LEGO publishes none; resellers list 50 g for the SPIKE version, possibly with packaging

no_load_rpm.note: LEGO Education sheet for the SPIKE Prime motor, the same motor in another colour: 185 rpm +/- 15 percent at 7.2 V

running_torque_nm.note: torque at maximum efficiency, 3.5 Ncm at 135 rpm

hole_pattern.why: LEGO states a cross hole on one side and a rotating disc with a cross hole and building interface on the other; no dimensioned drawing found

envelope.why: one box of the catalogue size with the output axis 16 mm from one end

rotor_inertia_kgm2.why: reflected rotor and gear inertia at the output, for the simulation

size_mm.note: 65 x 30 mm; holes 3.5 mm from each edge, so 58 x 23 mm centres

header_and_spacers_g.why: soldered 40-pin header, four spacers and screws

supply.value: 5 V 2.5 A micro USB, or from the Build HAT

mass_g.why: not published; a HAT of this size with four connectors and a barrel jack

spacer_mm.note: 'Attach 9 mm spacers to the bottom of the board'

supply.value: 8 V +/- 10 percent, 48 W, 5.5 x 2.1 mm barrel jack (the product brief says 7.2 V to 8.5 V); it also powers the Raspberry Pi

battery.why: the design README assumes the Build HAT's supported 8 V supply, which is a mains adapter: the robot is tethered. A battery is treated here as optional ballast.

battery_pack_g.why: six AA NiMH cells at 28 g in a holder, 7.2 V nominal, inside the brief's range; not tested

size_mm.note: holes 2.2 mm on 21 x 12.5 mm centres from the mechanical drawing

lego_brackets_g.why: four small right-angle brackets and fasteners of the LEGO edition

size_mm.why: no drawing published. The base plate carries an Arduino hole pattern, so it is at least Arduino sized; height to the tilt axis estimated.

mass_g.why: two micro servos, plates and fasteners; not published

technic.name: Technic axles, bushes, pins and bracket beams

axle_g_per_mm.why: cross axle section of about 13 mm2 in ABS

hardware_per_side_g.why: three axles, bushes and two pins

motor_bracket_g.why: two beams and pins per motor; layouts are not designed

gear_16t.value: module 1, 16 teeth, 16 mm pitch diameter, 7.8 mm wide
gear_16t.why: the Technic gear system uses module 1 with axles on an 8 mm grid; LEGO publishes no gear drawing

solid_fraction.why: same as the biped report: mostly shell at 20 percent infill

friction.why: printed PLA soles on a hard floor; generic tables give 0.2 to 0.5 for hard plastics. 0.2 and 0.8 are run as sensitivity
